Picture naming before and after therapy for word-finding difficulties

Source: R/data.R
aphasia_naming.Rd

16 people with chronic aphasia name 120 pictures each, twice before and once after eight weeks of cueing therapy. Half of each person's items were practised in therapy and half were not. Naming of treated items improves for almost every participant, and the two baselines do not differ. Naming of untreated items improves only for the five participants with a phonological profile: relatively good semantic processing and impaired phonological output. For mixed logistic regression of repeated measures, three-way interactions and generalisation in therapy studies.

Usage

aphasia_naming

Format

A tibble with 5760 rows and 6 columns:

participant

Participant ID, P01 to P16.

profile

"other" or "phonological".

item

Picture, numbered within participant (P01_001).

set

"untreated" or "treated".

session

"baseline 1", "baseline 2" or "post-therapy".

correct

1 if the picture was named correctly, 0 if not.

Source

data-raw/aphasia_naming.R

Details

True model: the logit of a correct response is p0 + i0 + post * gain. Participant intercepts p0 have mean -0.45 (SD 0.9) and item effects i0 SD 1.2. For treated items, gain is the participant's own gain (mean 1, SD 0.35). For untreated items it is 0.7 in the phonological profile and 0.05 otherwise, plus noise (SD 0.1). The design follows Best et al. (2013). In their 16 participants, naming of treated items rose from 43.5 to 62% correct, and only participants with relatively good semantic and impaired phonological processing generalised to untreated items. The number of items, the size of the subgroup and all data are simulated.

References

Best, W., Greenwood, A., Grassly, J., Herbert, R., Hickin, J. & Howard, D. (2013). Aphasia rehabilitation: Does generalisation from anomia therapy occur and is it predictable? A case series study. Cortex, 49(9), 2345-2357. doi:10.1016/j.cortex.2013.01.005

Examples

round(tapply(aphasia_naming$correct, aphasia_naming[c("set", "session")], mean), 2)
#>            session
#> set         baseline 1 baseline 2 post-therapy
#>   untreated       0.40       0.42         0.46
#>   treated         0.44       0.44         0.64
round(tapply(aphasia_naming$correct,
             aphasia_naming[c("profile", "set", "session")], mean), 2)
#> , , session = baseline 1
#> 
#>               set
#> profile        untreated treated
#>   other             0.41    0.47
#>   phonological      0.39    0.38
#> 
#> , , session = baseline 2
#> 
#>               set
#> profile        untreated treated
#>   other             0.43    0.47
#>   phonological      0.38    0.38
#> 
#> , , session = post-therapy
#> 
#>               set
#> profile        untreated treated
#>   other             0.43    0.66
#>   phonological      0.53    0.58
#> 
p01 <- subset(aphasia_naming, participant == "P01" & set == "treated" &
                session != "baseline 1")
mcnemar.test(table(before = p01$correct[p01$session == "baseline 2"],
                   after = p01$correct[p01$session == "post-therapy"]))
#> 
#> 	McNemar's Chi-squared test with continuity correction
#> 
#> data:  table(before = p01$correct[p01$session == "baseline 2"], after = p01$correct[p01$session == "post-therapy"])
#> McNemar's chi-squared = 14.815, df = 1, p-value = 0.0001186
#> 
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("lme4", quietly = TRUE)) {
  d <- subset(aphasia_naming, session != "baseline 1")
  m <- lme4::glmer(correct ~ session * set * profile + (1 | participant) + (1 | item),
                   data = d, family = binomial,
                   control = lme4::glmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa"))
  round(lme4::fixef(m), 2)
}
#>                                        (Intercept) 
#>                                              -0.34 
#>                                sessionpost-therapy 
#>                                              -0.03 
#>                                         settreated 
#>                                               0.20 
#>                                profilephonological 
#>                                              -0.29 
#>                     sessionpost-therapy:settreated 
#>                                               1.01 
#>            sessionpost-therapy:profilephonological 
#>                                               0.82 
#>                     settreated:profilephonological 
#>                                              -0.18 
#> sessionpost-therapy:settreated:profilephonological 
#>                                              -0.75
